selected_evidence.summary: Arch’s package metadata identifies Valkey as the Redis provider; compatibility binaries and redis.service exist, and the post-reboot service is active and listening on 10.100.11.10:6379.
AOF is configured with every-second fsync; live status reports successful writes, non-empty AOF files exist, and inventory:persistence-proof retained its value after node reboot.
The inventory ACL is defined and authenticates as inventory; anonymous access and writes outside inventory:* are denied both before and after reboot.

selected_evidence.summary: The node-generated credential is 64 characters long and /etc/redis-inventory.env remains root:root mode 0600 after reboot; no credential value was exposed.

The healthy baseline used boot ID 1db3db2e-dca8-44d6-8402-3b99605ae056; the reboot was acknowledged before disconnect; the recovered node reported boot ID 8018c0c9-ad0e-4b7a-81f3-a24540a0282b; Redis, its listener, inventory authentication, AOF status, credential permissions, and persisted data all recovered.

test -s /var/lib/valkey/appendonlydir/appendonly.aof.manifest
